items.title: How much confirmation friction actually pays for itself?
items.description: Illustrative model, not a measured study: represents the Team Settings 'Remove' button from the unit's audit. As you add confirmation steps (0 = instant delete like the original incident, higher = more friction — a hover-reveal, a named confirmation, a typed-name confirmation), accidental removals drop fast at first, then flatten out — while the average admin now spends more seconds completing a routine, intentional removal. Drag the slider to see where adding more friction stops meaningfully reducing mistakes and just slows everyone down.
items.compute: const accidentalRemovalsPer1000 = Math.round(40 * Math.exp(-params.confirmationSteps * 0.9) + 1); const secondsPerRoutineRemoval = Math.round((3 + params.confirmationSteps * 4) * 10) / 10; return { accidentalRemovalsPer1000, secondsPerRoutineRemoval };

outputs.label: Seconds added to a routine, intended removal
